title: MATH 23 Mastery Challenge: Fourier Transforms, Series & Z-Transforms
description: Comprehensive 22-question 4-quadrant companion mastery exam for MATH 23. Rigorously tests continuous Fourier transform pairs, trigonometric Fourier series symmetries, half-wave harmonic vanishing, Parseval energy, and discrete Z-transforms under timed board conditions.

questions.promptText: If a periodic waveform exhibits **Half-Wave Symmetry** ($f(t - T/2) = -f(t)$), what is true about its Fourier series harmonics?
questions.choiceA: All even harmonics are identically zero (only odd harmonics n = 1, 3, 5, ... exist).
questions.choiceB: All odd harmonics are identically zero.
questions.choiceD: The waveform has no sine terms.
questions.explanation: Integrating over half a period with $f(t - T/2) = -f(t)$ causes all even harmonics ($n = 2, 4, 6, \dots$) to cancel to zero, leaving only odd harmonics ($n = 1, 3, 5, \dots$).

questions.promptText: What is the **Continuous Fourier Transform** of the unit Dirac delta impulse **$\delta(t)$**?
questions.choiceA: 1 (a flat constant frequency spectrum for all ω)
questions.explanation: By definition: $\mathcal{F}\{\delta(t)\} = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \delta(t) e^{-j\omega t} dt = e^{-j\omega(0)} = 1$. The ideal impulse contains all frequencies equally.

questions.promptText: What does **Parseval's Energy Theorem** formally state for continuous-time signals?
questions.choiceA: The total energy in the time domain equals (1 / 2π) times the integrated spectral energy density in the frequency domain.
questions.choiceB: Energy is doubled when transforming into the frequency domain.
questions.choiceC: The DC component contains all the energy.
questions.choiceD: Energy depends on the phase angle.
questions.explanation: Parseval's relation expresses energy conservation: $\int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(t)|^2 dt = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^\infty |F(\omega)|^2 d\omega$.

questions.promptText: What is the **Unilateral Z-Transform** of the causal discrete unit step sequence **$u[n]$**?
questions.explanation: $\mathcal{Z}\{u[n]\} = \sum_{n=0}^\infty (1) z^{-n} = \frac{1}{1 - z^{-1}} = \frac{z}{z - 1}$ with Region of Convergence $|z| > 1$.

questions.promptText: If a periodic function is strictly an **Odd Function** ($f(-t) = -f(t)$), what terms appear in its trigonometric Fourier series?
questions.choiceA: Only sine terms (a₀ = 0 and aₙ = 0 for all n).
questions.choiceD: Only the constant DC term a₀.
questions.explanation: Because odd functions multiplied by even cosine functions remain odd, their symmetric integrals vanish ($a_n = 0$). Only sine harmonics ($b_n$) exist.

questions.promptText: What is the continuous Fourier transform of a rectangular time-domain pulse of width $T$ and height 1 centered at $t = 0$ ($\text{rect}(t/T)$)?
questions.explanation: Integrating $\int_{-T/2}^{T/2} e^{-j\omega t} dt = \frac{e^{-j\omega T/2} - e^{j\omega T/2}}{-j\omega} = \frac{2\sin(\omega T/2)}{\omega} = T \text{sinc}\left(\frac{\omega T}{2}\right)$.

questions.promptText: Find the continuous Fourier transform of the shifted impulse: $f(t) = \delta(t - 4)$.
questions.explanation: By the time-shifting property: $\mathcal{F}\{\delta(t - t_0)\} = e^{-j\omega t_0} \implies \mathcal{F}\{\delta(t - 4)\} = e^{-j 4\omega}$.

questions.promptText: Find the continuous Fourier transform of the causal decaying exponential $f(t) = e^{-3t} u(t)$.
questions.explanation: $\mathcal{F}\{e^{-at} u(t)\} = \int_0^\infty e^{-at} e^{-j\omega t} dt = \int_0^\infty e^{-(a + j\omega)t} dt = \frac{1}{a + j\omega} = \frac{1}{3 + j\omega}$.

questions.promptText: A periodic signal has a period of $T_0 = 20\text{ milliseconds}$ ($0.02\text{ s}$). Find its **fundamental angular frequency $\omega_0$** in $\text{rad/s}$.
questions.explanation: $\omega_0 = \frac{2\pi}{T_0} = \frac{2\pi}{0.02} = 100\pi \approx 314.159\text{ rad/s}$.

questions.promptText: Find the Z-transform of the geometric progression sequence $x[n] = \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^n u[n]$.
questions.explanation: $\mathcal{Z}\{a^n u[n]\} = \frac{z}{z - a} = \frac{z}{z - 1/3} = \frac{3z}{3z - 1}$ with ROC $|z| > 1/3$.

questions.promptText: Find the Z-transform of the delayed discrete unit impulse $x[n] = \delta[n - 2]$.
questions.explanation: By the discrete shifting property: $\mathcal{Z}\{\delta[n - k]\} = z^{-k} \implies \mathcal{Z}\{\delta[n - 2]\} = z^{-2} = \frac{1}{z^2}$.

questions.promptText: Using the Initial Value Theorem for Z-transforms ($x[0] = \lim_{z \to \infty} X(z)$), find $x[0]$ for $X(z) = \frac{2z + 1}{z - 0.5}$.
What is the continuous Fourier transform of the complex sinusoid $f(t) = e^{j 5 t}$?
questions.explanation: By the frequency shifting property on $\mathcal{F}\{1\} = 2\pi\delta(\omega)$: $\mathcal{F}\{e^{j\omega_0 t}\} = 2\pi\delta(\omega - \omega_0) = 2\pi\delta(\omega - 5)$.

questions.promptText: In digital signal processing, a causal discrete digital filter is described by the difference equation $y[n] = x[n] + 0.5 y[n - 1]$. What is its transfer function **$H(z) = \frac{Y(z)}{X(z)}$**?
questions.explanation: Taking Z-transforms: $Y(z) = X(z) + 0.5 z^{-1} Y(z) \implies Y(z)(1 - 0.5 z^{-1}) = X(z) \implies H(z) = \frac{1}{1 - 0.5 z^{-1}} = \frac{z}{z - 0.5}$.

questions.promptText: According to the **Nyquist Sampling Theorem**, what is the minimum sampling frequency required to digitize an analog telephone voice signal bandlimited to $f_{\max} = 4\text{ kHz}$ without aliasing distortion?
questions.explanation: The Nyquist minimum sampling rate is $f_s \ge 2 f_{\max} = 2(4\text{ kHz}) = 8\text{ kHz}$.

questions.promptText: A periodic square wave of amplitude $V_m$ has Fourier series $v(t) = \frac{4 V_m}{\pi}\left(\sin\omega_0 t + \frac{1}{3}\sin 3\omega_0 t + \frac{1}{5}\sin 5\omega_0 t + \dots\right)$. What is the amplitude of the **3rd harmonic** relative to the fundamental?
questions.explanation: The fundamental amplitude is $b_1 = \frac{4V_m}{\pi}$ and the 3rd harmonic is $b_3 = \frac{4V_m}{3\pi} = \frac{b_1}{3}$, so it is exactly one-third ($33.33\%$) of the fundamental.

questions.promptText: Find the inverse Z-transform of the causal transfer function $X(z) = \frac{z}{z - 2}$.
questions.explanation: From the standard Z-transform pair table: $\mathcal{Z}^{-1}\left\{\frac{z}{z - a}\right\} = a^n u[n] \implies \mathcal{Z}^{-1}\left\{\frac{z}{z - 2}\right\} = 2^n u[n]$.

questions.promptText: What is the **DC average value ($a_0 / 2$)** of a full-wave rectified sinusoidal AC voltage of peak amplitude $V_m$?
questions.explanation: The DC average of a full-wave rectified sine wave is $V_{dc} = \frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^\pi V_m\sin\theta d\theta = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \approx 0.6366 V_m$.

questions.promptText: What is the common sign trap when taking the continuous Fourier transform of a time-delayed signal $f(t - t_0)$?
questions.choiceA: Using a positive exponent e^(+jω t₀) instead of the correct negative exponent e^(-jω t₀).
questions.explanation: In continuous Fourier transforms, a positive delay $t - t_0$ introduces $e^{-j\omega t_0}$ (a negative phase lag $- \omega t_0$).

questions.promptText: When determining the Z-transform of $a^n u[n]$, what is the common algebraic confusion with continuous Laplace transforms?
questions.choiceA: Confusing the discrete form $\frac{z}{z - a}$ with the continuous Laplace form $\frac{1}{s - a}$.
questions.explanation: In continuous Laplace transforms, $\mathcal{L}\{e^{at}\} = \frac{1}{s - a}$ (constant numerator 1), whereas in discrete Z-transforms, $\mathcal{Z}\{a^n u[n]\} = \frac{z}{z - a}$ (numerator is variable $z$).

questions.promptText: If a periodic signal has Half-Wave Symmetry, what is the amplitude of its **4th harmonic ($n = 4$)** in 1 second?
questions.explanation: Half-wave symmetry guarantees all even harmonics ($n = 2, 4, 6, \dots$) are strictly zero in 1 second.

questions.promptText: Using the 2-second Z-transform shortcut, what is $\mathcal{Z}\{5^n u[n]\}$?
questions.explanation: $\mathcal{Z}\{a^n u[n]\} = \frac{z}{z - a} = \frac{z}{z - 5}$ in 1 second.
